source.citation: Bêty J, Giroux J-F, Gauthier G (2004) Individual variation in timing of migration: causes and reproductive consequences in greater snow geese (Anser caerulescens atlanticus). Behavioral Ecology and Sociobiology 57:1-8.
source.population: female greater snow geese, southern Quebec spring staging area to Bylot Island

ecological_interpretation: later departure can be partly offset by shorter migration duration; raw departure delay is not equivalent to downstream arrival delay

payoff_b_role.forbidden_reframing: do not convert the observed departure-duration correlation directly into D_eff or q_wait

direct_waiting_cost_anchor.source: Legagneux et al. 2012 / Grandmont et al. 2023
direct_waiting_cost_anchor.finding: captivity duration reduced later reproductive success or breeding propensity, whereas among detected breeders Grandmont et al. reported no detectable captivity-duration effect on arrival date or laying date
direct_waiting_cost_anchor.interpretation: waiting/perturbation can impose a direct carry-over cost that is not equivalent to residual timing delay and is not necessarily erased by downstream timing compensation
direct_waiting_cost_anchor.boundary: captivity combines elapsed time with capture, confinement and stress; do not numerically identify J from captivity duration alone
